title: Cavity sensor fault
shortDescription: The cavity temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
F1 on a Miele microwave means the NTC sensor that monitors cavity temperature reads open or shorted. The control locks out heating because it cannot enforce safe limits.

A power reset sometimes clears transient faults; persistent F1 needs sensor replacement.

fixSteps.title: Replace NTC
fixSteps.instruction: Access the cavity wall sensor and replace it.

whenToCallPro: Call Miele service for built-in models; sensor access may require removing the unit.

title: Over-temperature lockout
shortDescription: Cavity temperature exceeded the safe limit.
fullDescription:
F2 means the cavity reached a protective temperature, usually from running with little or no food, or from a blocked cooling fan.

Let the unit cool with the door open; repeat F2 codes need service.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Leave the door open for 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum the intake and exhaust grilles.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for built-in models that require removal to service the fan.

faq.a: Just wait for cool-down and restart.

title: Door switch fault
shortDescription: The door interlocks are not reporting a consistent state.
fullDescription:
F3 means one of the three safety interlock switches is misaligned or failed. Miele requires all three to change state together when the door opens.

The microwave locks out heating.

fixSteps.title: Check door
fixSteps.instruction: Open and close the door firmly; watch for sagging.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Interlock service should be done by a qualified technician.

whenToCallPro: Always call a pro; misaligned interlocks risk microwave leakage.

faq.a: No, but do not bypass the switches.

title: Touch panel fault
shortDescription: The touch panel reports a stuck key or is unresponsive.
fullDescription:
F4 appears when a key reads as pressed for too long at startup or during operation. Moisture under the panel is the most common cause.

Drying and cleaning often clears it.

fixSteps.title: Dry and clean
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the panel dry and leave unplugged for an hour.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new touch panel assembly if the fault persists.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if built-in installation blocks access.
videoSearchQuery: Miele microwave F4 touch panel fix

faq.q: Can I clean under the glass?
faq.a: Only by removing the panel; wipe the surface first.

title: Communication loss
shortDescription: The user interface lost contact with the main control.
fullDescription:
F5 means the UI and main PCB cannot exchange data over their internal bus. A loose connector or a failed board are typical causes.

The microwave will not start until restored.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: A technician should reseat or replace the affected harness.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for built-in units; removal is two-person work.

faq.a: Yes, the unit will not heat in this state.

title: Magnetron fault
shortDescription: The magnetron or HV circuit is not drawing the expected current.
fullDescription:
F10 indicates the high-voltage circuit powering the magnetron is abnormal. The magnetron itself, the HV diode, the capacitor, or the transformer may be at fault.

This is not DIY-safe because the HV capacitor stores lethal voltage.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and leave off until service.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Book a Miele technician to discharge the HV cap and test components.

whenToCallPro: Always; HV capacitors can kill even when unplugged.

faq.a: Yes, no radiation leakage with this fault.

title: HV transformer fault
shortDescription: The high-voltage transformer is not producing the expected output.
fullDescription:
F20 is thrown when the HV transformer output voltage or current falls outside firmware limits. Either the primary coil is open, the secondary shorted, or the control board is misreading feedback.

Always professional service.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Have a technician test and replace the transformer.

faq.a: Usually yes on Miele units; they are built to last.

title: Turntable motor fault
shortDescription: The turntable is not rotating as expected.
fullDescription:
F30 indicates the turntable motor is stalled, disconnected, or the feedback sensor is failing.

Usually debris under the tray; otherwise the motor needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Clean tray
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the tray and roller ring and clean the hub.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Access the motor from underneath and swap it.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for built-in units where motor access requires removal.

faq.a: Heating will be uneven; small items are okay.

title: Humidity sensor fault
shortDescription: The humidity sensor used for auto programs is out of range.
fullDescription:
F40 appears on Miele microwaves with auto-cook when the humidity sensor reads an invalid value. Grease buildup is the most common cause.

Manual cooking still works.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the sensor port with a damp microfiber.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the sensor module if cleaning fails.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the sensor lives behind the cavity liner.

faq.a: Yes, all manual programs still work.

title: Main control self-test failure
shortDescription: The main PCB failed its internal self-test.
fullDescription:
F50 is a fatal firmware fault. The main control board detected a memory or logic error at startup and will not operate.

A long power reset sometimes clears it; otherwise the board is replaced.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new main PCB if the fault returns.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for built-in units where removal is required.
videoSearchQuery: Miele microwave F50 main board fix

faq.a: Yes, a new board needs reprogramming.
